1	# Firma AI — HTTP Action Classifier
2	## End-to-End Technical Design Document
3	
4	### 1. Project overview
5	
6	Build a deterministic, security-focused Rust library that classifies outbound HTTP requests made by AI agents into predefined action classes.
7	
8	The system receives HTTP request metadata:
9	
10	- HTTP method
11	- Host
12	- URL path
13	
14	It compares this metadata against user-provided TOML mapping sets and returns the action class associated with the most specific matching rule.
15	
16	The classifier must remain provider-agnostic. It should not hardcode API providers, infer agent intent, or use an LLM to classify requests.
17	
18	The classifier is intended to be embedded inside a larger agent governance system. It does not perform HTTP interception, policy enforcement, or authorization itself.
19	
20	**Primary objective:** Given a collection of valid mapping rules and an HTTP request, consistently return the correct action class without ambiguity, panics, or unsafe fallback behavior.
21	
22	### 2. Scope and constraints
23	
24	#### In scope
25	
26	- TOML configuration parsing
27	- Configuration validation
28	- Multi-set loading
29	- Structured loading errors
30	- Rule compilation
31	- Host normalization
32	- Method validation
33	- Path normalization
34	- Exact and wildcard matching
35	- Rule specificity and precedence
36	- Cross-set conflict detection
37	- Deterministic classification
38	- Unit, integration, and robustness testing
39	- Thread-safe immutable classifier state
40	
41	#### Out of scope
42	
43	- Agent harnesses
44	- LLM inference
45	- HTTP interception
46	- HTTP servers or proxies
47	- Policy enforcement
48	- User authorization
49	- Databases
50	- Network requests
51	- Filesystem access
52	- CLI tools
53	- Session or reasoning analysis
54	
55	Do not expand beyond the Rust library described in the existing README.
56	
57	### 3. Existing public API
58	
59	Preserve the existing public API signatures.
60	
61	```rust
62	pub async fn load(
63	    sets: &[&str]
64	) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;
65	
66	impl Classifier {
67	    pub async fn classify(
68	        &self,
69	        method: &str,
70	        host: &str,
71	        path: &str
72	    ) -> Option<&str>;
73	}
74	```
75	
76	`load()` receives the raw text of one or more TOML mapping sets.
77	
78	`classify()` receives request metadata and returns a matching action class or `None`.
79	
80	Preserve the seven existing action classes:
81	
82	```rust
83	pub const ACTION_CLASSES: &[&str] = &[
84	    "payment.read",
85	    "payment.create",
86	    "payment.refund",
87	    "repo.read",
88	    "repo.write",
89	    "communication.external.send",
90	    "llm.inference",
91	];
92	```
93	
94	Do not add new classes.
95	
96	### 4. Architecture
97	
98	The library has two distinct execution phases.
99	
100	#### Phase A — Configuration loading
101	
102	```text
103	TOML Mapping Sets
104	        |
105	        v
106	Configuration Parser
107	        |
108	        v
109	Schema Validation
110	        |
111	        v
112	Semantic Validation
113	        |
114	        v
115	Rule Compilation
116	        |
117	        v
118	Cross-Set Conflict Detection
119	        |
120	        v
121	Immutable Classifier
122	```
123	
124	All configuration-related work should happen inside `load()`.
125	
126	The loader must reject invalid or ambiguous configurations before returning a usable classifier.
127	
128	#### Phase B — Request classification
129	
130	```text
131	HTTP Request Metadata
132	        |
133	        v
134	Request Normalization
135	        |
136	        v
137	Candidate Rule Matching
138	        |
139	        v
140	Specificity Comparison
141	        |
142	        v
143	Some(action_class) / None
144	```
145	
146	`classify()` must not parse TOML, perform I/O, or modify stored rules.
147	
148	The request path should remain lightweight and deterministic.
149	
150	### 5. Proposed module structure
151	
152	```text
153	Firma_take_home/
154	├── Cargo.toml
155	├── README.md
156	├── src/
157	│   ├── lib.rs
158	│   ├── config.rs
159	│   ├── normalize.rs
160	│   └── matcher.rs
161	└── tests/
162	    ├── example.rs
163	    ├── config_validation.rs
164	    ├── classification.rs
165	    ├── conflicts.rs
166	    └── security.rs
167	```
168	
169	#### `lib.rs`
170	
171	Owns the public API and integration between modules.
172	
173	Responsibilities:
174	
175	- Preserve `ACTION_CLASSES`.
176	- Define and expose `Classifier`.
177	- Define and expose `LoadError`.
178	- Implement `load()`.
179	- Implement `classify()`.
180	- Connect configuration compilation with matching.
181	
182	#### `config.rs`
183	
184	Owns configuration parsing and validation.
185	
186	Responsibilities:
187	
188	- Deserialize TOML.
189	- Validate required fields.
190	- Validate rule values.
191	- Reject unknown fields.
192	- Normalize configuration fields using agreed rules.
193	- Prepare validated rules.
194	- Preserve useful source metadata for errors.
195	
196	#### `normalize.rs`
197	
198	Owns request normalization.
199	
200	Responsibilities:
201	
202	- Normalize incoming hosts.
203	- Validate HTTP methods.
204	- Normalize paths according to the documented HTTP contract.
205	- Reject malformed or ambiguous inputs.
206	- Expose normalized request representations.
207	
208	#### `matcher.rs`
209	
210	Owns matching semantics and specificity.
211	
212	Responsibilities:
213	
214	- Match hosts and subdomains.
215	- Match HTTP methods.
216	- Match exact and wildcard paths.
217	- Calculate rule specificity.
218	- Compare matching rules.
219	- Determine whether two rule patterns overlap.
220	- Provide the shared matching logic needed for load-time conflict detection.
221	
222	The conflict detector must not independently reimplement matcher semantics.
223	
224	### 6. Configuration schema
225	
226	The TOML mapping structure is:
227	
228	```toml
229	format_version = 1
230	name = "Acme Payments"
231	description = "Acme API"
232	host = "acme.com"
233	
234	[[rules]]
235	method = "GET"
236	subdomain = "api"
237	path = "/v1/payment_intents"
238	action_class = "payment.read"
239	
240	[[rules]]
241	subdomain = "api"
242	path = "/v1/refunds/*"
243	action_class = "payment.refund"
244	```
245	
246	Use Serde to deserialize the configuration into strongly typed structures.
247	
248	```rust
249	#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
250	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
251	pub struct MappingSet {
252	    pub format_version: u32,
253	    pub name: String,
254	    pub description: Option<String>,
255	    pub host: String,
256	    pub rules: Vec<Rule>,
257	}
258	
259	#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
260	#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
261	pub struct Rule {
262	    pub method: Option<String>,
263	    pub subdomain: Option<String>,
264	    pub path: Option<String>,
265	    pub action_class: String,
266	}
267	```
268	
269	Both structures must reject unknown fields.
270	
271	Keep the raw configuration representation separate from the validated runtime representation.
272	
273	### 7. Configuration validation
274	
275	Validate every mapping set before compilation.
276	
277	#### Mapping-level validation
278	
279	Reject:
280	
281	- Invalid TOML syntax.
282	- Unknown or misspelled fields.
283	- Missing required fields.
284	- Empty required strings.
285	- Unsupported `format_version`.
286	- Invalid hostnames.
287	- Invalid rule arrays.
288	- Empty rule sets.
289	
290	Only `format_version = 1` is supported.
291	
292	An optional description may be absent or empty.
293	
294	#### Rule-level validation
295	
296	Reject:
297	
298	- Missing `action_class`.
299	- Empty `action_class`.
300	- An action class not present in `ACTION_CLASSES`.
301	- Invalid method tokens.
302	- Invalid subdomain formats.
303	- Invalid path patterns.
304	- Malformed percent encoding.
305	- Unsupported wildcard syntax.
306	- Ambiguous or unsafe normalized patterns.
307	
308	Optional rule fields:
309	
310	- `method`
311	- `subdomain`
312	- `path`
313	
314	Omitting a method or path means any valid method or path, respectively.
315	
316	Omitting a subdomain means the bare host only.
317	
318	#### Host validation
319	
320	Use an explicit ASCII DNS hostname contract.
321	
322	- Convert hostnames to lowercase.
323	- Reject empty labels.
324	- Reject invalid characters.
325	- Reject malformed leading or trailing hyphens.
326	- Reject embedded ports in configuration hostnames.
327	- Reject unsupported IP literals.
328	- Reject invalid wildcard placement.
329	- Preserve DNS label boundaries.
330	
331	Configuration `host` should represent the bare domain.
332	
333	Subdomain values must be either a valid single DNS label or `*`.
334	
335	#### Method validation
336	
337	- HTTP method tokens are case-sensitive.
338	- Reject invalid token characters.
339	- Reject whitespace.
340	- Reject empty strings.
341	- Do not silently uppercase methods.
342	- A missing method means any valid method.
343	
344	#### Path validation
345	
346	- Explicit path patterns must begin with `/`.
347	- `*` is the only supported wildcard character.
348	- Reject malformed percent encoding.
349	- Reject encoded separators that create ambiguous path interpretations.
350	- Apply the same canonicalization contract to configuration literals and request paths.
351	- Do not perform arbitrary percent decoding.
352	- Preserve duplicate slashes and trailing slashes.
353	- Reject patterns that cannot be represented safely by the matcher.
354	
355	### 8. Internal compiled representation
356	
357	The runtime classifier should not retain raw TOML structures as its primary matching format.
358	
359	Introduce a validated internal representation.
360	
361	Conceptually:
362	
363	```rust
364	struct CompiledRule {
365	    host: HostMatcher,
366	    method: MethodMatcher,
367	    path: PathMatcher,
368	    action_class: &'static str,
369	    specificity: Specificity,
370	}
371	```
372	
373	Possible internal matcher types:
374	
375	```rust
376	enum HostMatcher {
377	    Bare(String),
378	    ExactSubdomain {
379	        base: String,
380	        subdomain: String,
381	    },
382	    WildcardSubdomain {
383	        base: String,
384	    },
385	}
386	
387	enum MethodMatcher {
388	    Any,
389	    Exact(String),
390	}
391	
392	enum PathMatcher {
393	    Any,
394	    Exact(String),
395	    Wildcard(CompiledPattern),
396	}
397	```
398	
399	The precise types may change based on the matcher implementation, but parsing and matching must agree on one shared contract.
400	
401	`Specificity` should be a structured value with an explicitly defined ordering.
402	
403	Since the action classes are a fixed constant list, compiled rules may reference the corresponding static string rather than repeatedly allocating identical class values.
404	
405	Preserve mapping-set index, mapping name, and rule index during loading so errors can identify their sources.
406	
407	### 9. HTTP request normalization
408	
409	Normalize incoming request metadata before matching.
410	
411	#### Host
412	
413	- Lowercase ASCII hostnames.
414	- Accept valid numeric ports and remove them.
415	- Remove one trailing DNS dot.
416	- Reject empty or malformed hosts.
417	- Reject userinfo.
418	- Reject invalid domain labels.
419	- Reject unsupported IP literal representations.
420	- Preserve subdomain boundaries.
421	
422	`api.acme.com` must never match `evilapi.acme.com` unless explicitly configured to do so.
423	
424	#### Method
425	
426	- Preserve case.
427	- Validate according to HTTP token syntax.
428	- Reject malformed tokens.
429	- Do not infer method semantics.
430	
431	#### Path
432	
433	- Empty path becomes `/`.
434	- Remove query strings and fragments before matching.
435	- Require a leading `/` for nonempty paths.
436	- Preserve duplicate slashes.
437	- Preserve trailing slashes.
438	- Normalize unambiguous dot segments.
439	- Handle encoded dot segments consistently.
440	- Reject malformed percent encoding.
441	- Reject encoded `/` and `\` where interpretations are ambiguous.
442	- Avoid double decoding.
443	- Reject unsupported or ambiguous representations.
444	
445	Document the normalization contract clearly.
446	
447	HTTP clients and upstream servers may interpret some paths differently. The classifier cannot guarantee semantic equivalence across every upstream service using only method, host, and path. Prefer conservative rejection when interpretation is uncertain.
448	
449	### 10. Rule matching
450	
451	#### Host matching
452	
453	For `host = "acme.com"`:
454	
455	- Omitted subdomain matches `acme.com`.
456	- `subdomain = "api"` matches `api.acme.com`.
457	- `subdomain = "*"` matches any nonempty subdomain.
458	- Wildcard subdomains may span multiple DNS label levels.
459	- Wildcard subdomains do not match the bare host.
460	- Exact subdomains take priority over wildcard subdomains when both match.
461	
462	#### Method matching
463	
464	- Exact methods must match case-sensitively.
465	- An omitted method matches any valid method.
466	- Explicit methods outrank omitted methods when higher-priority dimensions are equivalent.
467	
468	#### Path matching
469	
470	- Exact paths match exactly after normalization.
471	- `*` matches zero or more characters, including `/`.
472	- Multiple wildcards are permitted.
473	- An omitted path matches every valid normalized path.
474	- Explicit paths outrank omitted paths.
475	
476	Example:
477	
478	`/v1/refunds/*` matches:
479	
480	- `/v1/refunds/re_123`
481	- `/v1/refunds/a/b/c`
482	- `/v1/refunds/`
483	
484	It does not match `/v1/refunds`.
485	
486	### 11. Specificity ordering
487	
488	Use a deterministic lexicographic ordering.
489	
490	The order is:
491	
492	1. Host specificity.
493	2. Path specificity.
494	3. Method specificity.
495	
496	Host specificity:
497	
498	- Exact subdomain takes priority over wildcard subdomain.
499	- Bare-host rules match only the bare host.
500	
501	Path specificity:
502	
503	- Exact path over wildcard path.
504	- Wildcard path over omitted path.
505	- Among wildcard patterns, prefer more literal characters.
506	- Then prefer fewer wildcards.
507	- Then prefer greater literal-prefix length.
508	
509	Method specificity:
510	
511	- Explicit method over omitted method.
512	
513	Do not use source-file ordering or insertion ordering as a tiebreaker.
514	
515	If two matching rules have identical specificity and different action classes, loading must have rejected the ambiguity beforehand.
516	
517	### 12. Multiple mapping sets
518	
519	`load()` must support multiple TOML mapping sets in the same call.
520	
521	Example:
522	
523	```rust
524	let classifier = load(&[
525	    payments_mapping,
526	    github_mapping,
527	    llm_mapping,
528	]).await?;
529	```
530	
531	Requirements:
532	
533	- Parse each set independently.
534	- Validate each set independently.
535	- Compile all accepted rules into a shared collection.
536	- Detect conflicts within and across mapping sets.
537	- Reject invalid combinations before exposing the classifier.
538	- Never give a mapping set priority because it was loaded first.
539	- Treat duplicate equivalent rules returning the same action class as harmless; they may be deduplicated.
540	
541	A change in the ordering of mapping sets must not change classification results.
542	
543	### 13. Conflict detection
544	
545	Conflict detection happens during `load()`.
546	
547	A conflict occurs when two rules:
548	
549	1. Can match at least one identical valid HTTP request.
550	2. Have the same specificity for that request.
551	3. Return different action classes.
552	
553	Example:
554	
555	```toml
556	method = "POST"
557	path = "/v1/refunds/*"
558	action_class = "payment.refund"
559	```
560	
561	versus:
562	
563	```toml
564	method = "POST"
565	path = "/v1/refunds/*"
566	action_class = "payment.read"
567	```
568	
569	Reject the combined configuration.
570	
571	Conflicts are not limited to identical rule strings.
572	
573	For example, two different wildcard patterns may overlap and have equal specificity.
574	
575	The matcher module should provide shared primitives for:
576	
577	- Checking whether two host matchers can overlap.
578	- Checking whether two method matchers can overlap.
579	- Checking whether two path patterns can overlap.
580	- Comparing rule specificity.
581	
582	The configuration loader should call these primitives rather than implement its own matching semantics.
583	
584	A conservative conflict detector must not silently accept an unresolved ambiguity. If exact overlap checking is not implemented for a supported pattern type, either restrict that pattern type during validation or reject potentially conflicting patterns with an explicit error.
585	
586	Avoid silently selecting the first encountered rule.
587	
588	### 14. Structured error handling
589	
590	Replace the placeholder `LoadError`.
591	
592	Use a `thiserror`-based enum with variants corresponding to major failure categories.
593	
594	Suggested categories:
595	
596	- Invalid TOML.
597	- Unsupported format version.
598	- Missing or empty required value.
599	- Invalid hostname.
600	- Invalid method.
601	- Invalid subdomain.
602	- Invalid path pattern.
603	- Invalid action class.
604	- Empty rule set.
605	- Conflicting rules.
606	- Unsupported or ambiguous configuration.
607	
608	Every error should identify the relevant mapping set by input index and, when available, its declared name.
609	
610	Rule-specific errors should include the rule index.
611	
612	Conflict errors should identify both rules and both mapping sets.
613	
614	For example:
615	
616	```text
617	Mapping set 2 "Acme Payments", rule 3:
618	Unknown action class "payment.delete"
619	
620	Mapping sets 1 rule 2 and 3 rule 4:
621	Conflicting classifications for overlapping requests
622	```
623	
624	Avoid using `unwrap()` or `expect()` for user-provided configuration.
625	
626	### 15. Classifier runtime behavior
627	
628	`classify()` should:
629	
630	1. Validate and normalize request inputs.
631	2. Return `None` immediately if normalization fails.
632	3. Compare normalized inputs against compiled rules.
633	4. Identify every applicable candidate or maintain the best candidate while scanning.
634	5. Select the highest-specificity match.
635	6. Return its action class.
636	7. Return `None` if no rule matches.
637	
638	It must not:
639	
640	- Parse TOML.
641	- Access a database.
642	- Make network requests.
643	- Perform filesystem I/O.
644	- Mutate shared classifier state.
645	- Depend on a coding agent or LLM.
646	- Panic on malformed requests.
647	
648	For the expected scope, an immutable vector of compiled rules with a linear scan is an acceptable initial implementation.
649	
650	More elaborate indexing should only be introduced if benchmarks demonstrate a benefit.
651	
652	### 16. Concurrency and performance
653	
654	The library will be used inside HTTP handlers.
655	
656	Requirements:
657	
658	- `Classifier` must be `Send + Sync`.
659	- Rules remain immutable after loading.
660	- No locks should be necessary for ordinary classification.
661	- Avoid expensive preprocessing on every request.
662	- Precompute specificity metadata during loading.
663	- Compile path wildcard representations during loading.
664	- Keep classification deterministic under concurrent requests.
665	- Avoid unnecessary allocations where practical.
666	
667	The public functions remain asynchronous because the starter API requires it, but internal parsing and matching do not require asynchronous tasks.
668	
669	If practical, verify concurrent classifications through a Tokio test using a shared `Arc<Classifier>`.
670	
671	### 17. Testing strategy
672	
673	#### Configuration parsing tests
674	
675	Cover:
676	
677	- Valid mapping files.
678	- Invalid TOML syntax.
679	- Unknown top-level keys.
680	- Unknown rule-level keys.
681	- Missing required fields.
682	- Empty required strings.
683	- Unsupported format versions.
684	- Optional fields omitted.
685	- Empty rules.
686	- Invalid action classes.
687	- Malformed methods.
688	- Malformed hostnames.
689	- Invalid subdomains.
690	- Invalid paths.
691	
692	#### Matching tests
693	
694	Cover:
695	
696	- Exact host matching.
697	- Bare hosts.
698	- Exact subdomains.
699	- Wildcard subdomains.
700	- Nested subdomains.
701	- Exact methods.
702	- Omitted methods.
703	- Exact paths.
704	- Wildcard paths.
705	- Multiple path wildcards.
706	- Omitted paths.
707	- Unmatched requests.
708	
709	#### Specificity tests
710	
711	Cover:
712	
713	- Exact host versus wildcard host.
714	- Exact path versus wildcard path.
715	- Wildcard path specificity comparisons.
716	- Explicit method versus omitted method.
717	- Multiple simultaneously matching rules.
718	- Equal-specificity ties.
719	- Independent results when loading sets in different orders.
720	
721	#### Conflict tests
722	
723	Cover:
724	
725	- Identical rules with different classes.
726	- Overlapping wildcard rules with different classes.
727	- Conflicts inside one set.
728	- Conflicts across multiple sets.
729	- Duplicate rules with the same class.
730	- Overlapping rules where one has higher specificity.
731	- Rules matching different hosts that should not conflict.
732	
733	#### Normalization and security tests
734	
735	Cover:
736	
737	- Host casing.
738	- Host ports.
739	- Trailing host dots.
740	- Host suffix bypass attempts.
741	- Malformed userinfo.
742	- HTTP method casing.
743	- Invalid method tokens.
744	- Empty paths.
745	- Query strings.
746	- Fragments.
747	- Duplicate slashes.
748	- Trailing slashes.
749	- Literal dot segments.
750	- Encoded dot segments.
751	- Encoded path separators.
752	- Invalid percent sequences.
753	- Unicode paths.
754	- Arbitrary malformed input.
755	
756	#### Robustness tests
757	
758	Use property-based testing or fuzz-style generated inputs to confirm:
759	
760	- `classify()` never panics.
761	- Classification remains deterministic.
762	- Rule ordering does not affect results.
763	- Malformed input does not unexpectedly map to a valid action class.
764	- Concurrent classification does not mutate shared state.
765	
766	Maintain all four existing example tests.
767	
768	### 18. Multi-agent development plan
769	
770	Two coding agents are working concurrently.
771	
772	#### Agent 1 — Configuration and compilation
773	
774	Ownership:
775	
776	- `config.rs`
777	- Parsing and configuration validation tests
778	- Configuration-related error design
779	- Validated rule construction
780	- Loader-related conflict detection integration
781	
782	Responsibilities:
783	
784	- Deserialize TOML.
785	- Reject invalid configurations.
786	- Verify allowed action classes.
787	- Build validated mapping data.
788	- Prepare source metadata for errors.
789	- Coordinate compiled rule interfaces with the matcher.
790	
791	Do not independently implement request matching.
792	
793	#### Agent 2 — Normalization and matching
794	
795	Ownership:
796	
797	- `normalize.rs`
798	- `matcher.rs`
799	- Normalization and matching unit tests
800	
801	Responsibilities:
802	
803	- Implement request normalization.
804	- Implement exact and wildcard matching.
805	- Implement specificity ordering.
806	- Implement overlap detection primitives.
807	- Expose interfaces for compiled rule evaluation.
808	
809	Do not independently parse TOML.
810	
811	#### Integration phase
812	
813	After both agents finish:
814	
815	- Review both module contracts.
816	- Establish shared compiled-rule types.
817	- Connect parser output to matcher input.
818	- Implement the public `load()` function.
819	- Implement the public `classify()` function.
820	- Connect conflict detection to loading.
821	- Run integration tests.
822	- Resolve mismatches between modules.
823	- Verify order independence and security assumptions.
824	
825	Use separate Git worktrees or branches for parallel agents where possible, and integrate intentionally rather than allowing simultaneous edits to shared files.
826	
827	### 19. Verification and acceptance criteria
828	
829	The implementation is complete when:
830	
831	- The original public API is unchanged.
832	- All valid TOML mapping sets load successfully.
833	- Invalid configurations produce useful errors.
834	- Only predefined action classes can be returned.
835	- Multiple mapping sets work without ordering precedence.
836	- Conflicting rules are rejected.
837	- The most specific matching rule is selected deterministically.
838	- Request normalization is consistent and documented.
839	- Malformed inputs return `None` without panicking.
840	- Classification requires no network, filesystem, or external services.
841	- `Classifier` is safe for concurrent use.
842	- The four starter tests pass.
843	- Additional unit and integration tests pass.
844	- The crate builds without warnings.
845	- Clippy reports no warnings under the selected lint configuration.
846	
847	Run:
848	
849	```bash
850	cargo fmt --check
851	cargo build
852	cargo test
853	cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
854	```
855	
856	### 20. Submission requirements
857	
858	Preserve the complete raw coding-agent session transcripts for all sessions used during development.
859	
860	Include all instruction files provided to the agents, including any `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or skill files created for this project.
861	
862	Do not sanitize, redact, or summarize the required raw transcripts.
863	
864	Review the recorded sessions for unintended exposure of credentials before using any external services during development. Avoid introducing secrets into the take-home workflow.
865	
866	Ensure the repository and any accompanying documentation accurately describe the implemented behavior and its limitations.
867	
868	### 21. Final engineering principles
869	
870	The solution should prioritize:
871	
872	1. Correctness over cleverness.
873	2. Security over permissive matching.
874	3. Deterministic behavior over implicit precedence.
875	4. Explicit validation over silent correction.
876	5. Immutable state over shared mutable runtime state.
877	6. Clear module boundaries over unnecessary abstraction.
878	7. Comprehensive adversarial testing over happy-path testing alone.
879	
880	The ultimate goal is a small, production-quality classification component whose behavior can be explained and defended for every supported input.
881	
882	**The classifier is not expected to understand an agent's reasoning. It must reliably classify observable HTTP operations according to explicitly configured mapping rules.**

# Firma AI — HTTP Action Classifier
## End-to-End Technical Design Document

### 1. Project overview

Build a deterministic, security-focused Rust library that classifies outbound HTTP requests made by AI agents into predefined action classes.

The system receives HTTP request metadata:

- HTTP method
- Host
- URL path

It compares this metadata against user-provided TOML mapping sets and returns the action class associated with the most specific matching rule.

The classifier must remain provider-agnostic. It should not hardcode API providers, infer agent intent, or use an LLM to classify requests.

The classifier is intended to be embedded inside a larger agent governance system. It does not perform HTTP interception, policy enforcement, or authorization itself.

**Primary objective:** Given a collection of valid mapping rules and an HTTP request, consistently return the correct action class without ambiguity, panics, or unsafe fallback behavior.

### 2. Scope and constraints

#### In scope

- TOML configuration parsing
- Configuration validation
- Multi-set loading
- Structured loading errors
- Rule compilation
- Host normalization
- Method validation
- Path normalization
- Exact and wildcard matching
- Rule specificity and precedence
- Cross-set conflict detection
- Deterministic classification
- Unit, integration, and robustness testing
- Thread-safe immutable classifier state

#### Out of scope

- Agent harnesses
- LLM inference
- HTTP interception
- HTTP servers or proxies
- Policy enforcement
- User authorization
- Databases
- Network requests
- Filesystem access
- CLI tools
- Session or reasoning analysis

Do not expand beyond the Rust library described in the existing README.

### 3. Existing public API

Preserve the existing public API signatures.

```rust
pub async fn load(
    sets: &[&str]
) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;

impl Classifier {
    pub async fn classify(
        &self,
        method: &str,
        host: &str,
        path: &str
    ) -> Option<&str>;
}
```

`load()` receives the raw text of one or more TOML mapping sets.

`classify()` receives request metadata and returns a matching action class or `None`.

Preserve the seven existing action classes:

```rust
pub const ACTION_CLASSES: &[&str] = &[
    "payment.read",
    "payment.create",
    "payment.refund",
    "repo.read",
    "repo.write",
    "communication.external.send",
    "llm.inference",
];
```

Do not add new classes.

### 4. Architecture

The library has two distinct execution phases.

#### Phase A — Configuration loading

```text
TOML Mapping Sets
        |
        v
Configuration Parser
        |
        v
Schema Validation
        |
        v
Semantic Validation
        |
        v
Rule Compilation
        |
        v
Cross-Set Conflict Detection
        |
        v
Immutable Classifier
```

All configuration-related work should happen inside `load()`.

The loader must reject invalid or ambiguous configurations before returning a usable classifier.

#### Phase B — Request classification

```text
HTTP Request Metadata
        |
        v
Request Normalization
        |
        v
Candidate Rule Matching
        |
        v
Specificity Comparison
        |
        v
Some(action_class) / None
```

`classify()` must not parse TOML, perform I/O, or modify stored rules.

The request path should remain lightweight and deterministic.

### 5. Proposed module structure

```text
Firma_take_home/
├── Cargo.toml
├── README.md
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs
│   ├── config.rs
│   ├── normalize.rs
│   └── matcher.rs
└── tests/
    ├── example.rs
    ├── config_validation.rs
    ├── classification.rs
    ├── conflicts.rs
    └── security.rs
```

#### `lib.rs`

Owns the public API and integration between modules.

Responsibilities:

- Preserve `ACTION_CLASSES`.
- Define and expose `Classifier`.
- Define and expose `LoadError`.
- Implement `load()`.
- Implement `classify()`.
- Connect configuration compilation with matching.

#### `config.rs`

Owns configuration parsing and validation.

Responsibilities:

- Deserialize TOML.
- Validate required fields.
- Validate rule values.
- Reject unknown fields.
- Normalize configuration fields using agreed rules.
- Prepare validated rules.
- Preserve useful source metadata for errors.

#### `normalize.rs`

Owns request normalization.

Responsibilities:

- Normalize incoming hosts.
- Validate HTTP methods.
- Normalize paths according to the documented HTTP contract.
- Reject malformed or ambiguous inputs.
- Expose normalized request representations.

#### `matcher.rs`

Owns matching semantics and specificity.

Responsibilities:

- Match hosts and subdomains.
- Match HTTP methods.
- Match exact and wildcard paths.
- Calculate rule specificity.
- Compare matching rules.
- Determine whether two rule patterns overlap.
- Provide the shared matching logic needed for load-time conflict detection.

The conflict detector must not independently reimplement matcher semantics.

### 6. Configuration schema

The TOML mapping structure is:

```toml
format_version = 1
name = "Acme Payments"
description = "Acme API"
host = "acme.com"

[[rules]]
method = "GET"
subdomain = "api"
path = "/v1/payment_intents"
action_class = "payment.read"

[[rules]]
subdomain = "api"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.refund"
```

Use Serde to deserialize the configuration into strongly typed structures.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct MappingSet {
    pub format_version: u32,
    pub name: String,
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub host: String,
    pub rules: Vec<Rule>,
}

#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub method: Option<String>,
    pub subdomain: Option<String>,
    pub path: Option<String>,
    pub action_class: String,
}
```

Both structures must reject unknown fields.

Keep the raw configuration representation separate from the validated runtime representation.

### 7. Configuration validation

Validate every mapping set before compilation.

#### Mapping-level validation

Reject:

- Invalid TOML syntax.
- Unknown or misspelled fields.
- Missing required fields.
- Empty required strings.
- Unsupported `format_version`.
- Invalid hostnames.
- Invalid rule arrays.
- Empty rule sets.

Only `format_version = 1` is supported.

An optional description may be absent or empty.

#### Rule-level validation

Reject:

- Missing `action_class`.
- Empty `action_class`.
- An action class not present in `ACTION_CLASSES`.
- Invalid method tokens.
- Invalid subdomain formats.
- Invalid path patterns.
- Malformed percent encoding.
- Unsupported wildcard syntax.
- Ambiguous or unsafe normalized patterns.

Optional rule fields:

- `method`
- `subdomain`
- `path`

Omitting a method or path means any valid method or path, respectively.

Omitting a subdomain means the bare host only.

#### Host validation

Use an explicit ASCII DNS hostname contract.

- Convert hostnames to lowercase.
- Reject empty labels.
- Reject invalid characters.
- Reject malformed leading or trailing hyphens.
- Reject embedded ports in configuration hostnames.
- Reject unsupported IP literals.
- Reject invalid wildcard placement.
- Preserve DNS label boundaries.

Configuration `host` should represent the bare domain.

Subdomain values must be either a valid single DNS label or `*`.

#### Method validation

- HTTP method tokens are case-sensitive.
- Reject invalid token characters.
- Reject whitespace.
- Reject empty strings.
- Do not silently uppercase methods.
- A missing method means any valid method.

#### Path validation

- Explicit path patterns must begin with `/`.
- `*` is the only supported wildcard character.
- Reject malformed percent encoding.
- Reject encoded separators that create ambiguous path interpretations.
- Apply the same canonicalization contract to configuration literals and request paths.
- Do not perform arbitrary percent decoding.
- Preserve duplicate slashes and trailing slashes.
- Reject patterns that cannot be represented safely by the matcher.

### 8. Internal compiled representation

The runtime classifier should not retain raw TOML structures as its primary matching format.

Introduce a validated internal representation.

Conceptually:

```rust
struct CompiledRule {
    host: HostMatcher,
    method: MethodMatcher,
    path: PathMatcher,
    action_class: &'static str,
    specificity: Specificity,
}
```

Possible internal matcher types:

```rust
enum HostMatcher {
    Bare(String),
    ExactSubdomain {
        base: String,
        subdomain: String,
    },
    WildcardSubdomain {
        base: String,
    },
}

enum MethodMatcher {
    Any,
    Exact(String),
}

enum PathMatcher {
    Any,
    Exact(String),
    Wildcard(CompiledPattern),
}
```

The precise types may change based on the matcher implementation, but parsing and matching must agree on one shared contract.

`Specificity` should be a structured value with an explicitly defined ordering.

Since the action classes are a fixed constant list, compiled rules may reference the corresponding static string rather than repeatedly allocating identical class values.

Preserve mapping-set index, mapping name, and rule index during loading so errors can identify their sources.

### 9. HTTP request normalization

Normalize incoming request metadata before matching.

#### Host

- Lowercase ASCII hostnames.
- Accept valid numeric ports and remove them.
- Remove one trailing DNS dot.
- Reject empty or malformed hosts.
- Reject userinfo.
- Reject invalid domain labels.
- Reject unsupported IP literal representations.
- Preserve subdomain boundaries.

`api.acme.com` must never match `evilapi.acme.com` unless explicitly configured to do so.

#### Method

- Preserve case.
- Validate according to HTTP token syntax.
- Reject malformed tokens.
- Do not infer method semantics.

#### Path

- Empty path becomes `/`.
- Remove query strings and fragments before matching.
- Require a leading `/` for nonempty paths.
- Preserve duplicate slashes.
- Preserve trailing slashes.
- Normalize unambiguous dot segments.
- Handle encoded dot segments consistently.
- Reject malformed percent encoding.
- Reject encoded `/` and `\` where interpretations are ambiguous.
- Avoid double decoding.
- Reject unsupported or ambiguous representations.

Document the normalization contract clearly.

HTTP clients and upstream servers may interpret some paths differently. The classifier cannot guarantee semantic equivalence across every upstream service using only method, host, and path. Prefer conservative rejection when interpretation is uncertain.

### 10. Rule matching

#### Host matching

For `host = "acme.com"`:

- Omitted subdomain matches `acme.com`.
- `subdomain = "api"` matches `api.acme.com`.
- `subdomain = "*"` matches any nonempty subdomain.
- Wildcard subdomains may span multiple DNS label levels.
- Wildcard subdomains do not match the bare host.
- Exact subdomains take priority over wildcard subdomains when both match.

#### Method matching

- Exact methods must match case-sensitively.
- An omitted method matches any valid method.
- Explicit methods outrank omitted methods when higher-priority dimensions are equivalent.

#### Path matching

- Exact paths match exactly after normalization.
- `*` matches zero or more characters, including `/`.
- Multiple wildcards are permitted.
- An omitted path matches every valid normalized path.
- Explicit paths outrank omitted paths.

Example:

`/v1/refunds/*` matches:

- `/v1/refunds/re_123`
- `/v1/refunds/a/b/c`
- `/v1/refunds/`

It does not match `/v1/refunds`.

### 11. Specificity ordering

Use a deterministic lexicographic ordering.

The order is:

1. Host specificity.
2. Path specificity.
3. Method specificity.

Host specificity:

- Exact subdomain takes priority over wildcard subdomain.
- Bare-host rules match only the bare host.

Path specificity:

- Exact path over wildcard path.
- Wildcard path over omitted path.
- Among wildcard patterns, prefer more literal characters.
- Then prefer fewer wildcards.
- Then prefer greater literal-prefix length.

Method specificity:

- Explicit method over omitted method.

Do not use source-file ordering or insertion ordering as a tiebreaker.

If two matching rules have identical specificity and different action classes, loading must have rejected the ambiguity beforehand.

### 12. Multiple mapping sets

`load()` must support multiple TOML mapping sets in the same call.

Example:

```rust
let classifier = load(&[
    payments_mapping,
    github_mapping,
    llm_mapping,
]).await?;
```

Requirements:

- Parse each set independently.
- Validate each set independently.
- Compile all accepted rules into a shared collection.
- Detect conflicts within and across mapping sets.
- Reject invalid combinations before exposing the classifier.
- Never give a mapping set priority because it was loaded first.
- Treat duplicate equivalent rules returning the same action class as harmless; they may be deduplicated.

A change in the ordering of mapping sets must not change classification results.

### 13. Conflict detection

Conflict detection happens during `load()`.

A conflict occurs when two rules:

1. Can match at least one identical valid HTTP request.
2. Have the same specificity for that request.
3. Return different action classes.

Example:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.refund"
```

versus:

```toml
method = "POST"
path = "/v1/refunds/*"
action_class = "payment.read"
```

Reject the combined configuration.

Conflicts are not limited to identical rule strings.

For example, two different wildcard patterns may overlap and have equal specificity.

The matcher module should provide shared primitives for:

- Checking whether two host matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two method matchers can overlap.
- Checking whether two path patterns can overlap.
- Comparing rule specificity.

The configuration loader should call these primitives rather than implement its own matching semantics.

A conservative conflict detector must not silently accept an unresolved ambiguity. If exact overlap checking is not implemented for a supported pattern type, either restrict that pattern type during validation or reject potentially conflicting patterns with an explicit error.

Avoid silently selecting the first encountered rule.

### 14. Structured error handling

Replace the placeholder `LoadError`.

Use a `thiserror`-based enum with variants corresponding to major failure categories.

Suggested categories:

- Invalid TOML.
- Unsupported format version.
- Missing or empty required value.
- Invalid hostname.
- Invalid method.
- Invalid subdomain.
- Invalid path pattern.
- Invalid action class.
- Empty rule set.
- Conflicting rules.
- Unsupported or ambiguous configuration.

Every error should identify the relevant mapping set by input index and, when available, its declared name.

Rule-specific errors should include the rule index.

Conflict errors should identify both rules and both mapping sets.

For example:

```text
Mapping set 2 "Acme Payments", rule 3:
Unknown action class "payment.delete"

Mapping sets 1 rule 2 and 3 rule 4:
Conflicting classifications for overlapping requests
```

Avoid using `unwrap()` or `expect()` for user-provided configuration.

### 15. Classifier runtime behavior

`classify()` should:

1. Validate and normalize request inputs.
2. Return `None` immediately if normalization fails.
3. Compare normalized inputs against compiled rules.
4. Identify every applicable candidate or maintain the best candidate while scanning.
5. Select the highest-specificity match.
6. Return its action class.
7. Return `None` if no rule matches.

It must not:

- Parse TOML.
- Access a database.
- Make network requests.
- Perform filesystem I/O.
- Mutate shared classifier state.
- Depend on a coding agent or LLM.
- Panic on malformed requests.

For the expected scope, an immutable vector of compiled rules with a linear scan is an acceptable initial implementation.

More elaborate indexing should only be introduced if benchmarks demonstrate a benefit.

### 16. Concurrency and performance

The library will be used inside HTTP handlers.

Requirements:

- `Classifier` must be `Send + Sync`.
- Rules remain immutable after loading.
- No locks should be necessary for ordinary classification.
- Avoid expensive preprocessing on every request.
- Precompute specificity metadata during loading.
- Compile path wildcard representations during loading.
- Keep classification deterministic under concurrent requests.
- Avoid unnecessary allocations where practical.

The public functions remain asynchronous because the starter API requires it, but internal parsing and matching do not require asynchronous tasks.

If practical, verify concurrent classifications through a Tokio test using a shared `Arc<Classifier>`.

### 17. Testing strategy

#### Configuration parsing tests

Cover:

- Valid mapping files.
- Invalid TOML syntax.
- Unknown top-level keys.
- Unknown rule-level keys.
- Missing required fields.
- Empty required strings.
- Unsupported format versions.
- Optional fields omitted.
- Empty rules.
- Invalid action classes.
- Malformed methods.
- Malformed hostnames.
- Invalid subdomains.
- Invalid paths.

#### Matching tests

Cover:

- Exact host matching.
- Bare hosts.
- Exact subdomains.
- Wildcard subdomains.
- Nested subdomains.
- Exact methods.
- Omitted methods.
- Exact paths.
- Wildcard paths.
- Multiple path wildcards.
- Omitted paths.
- Unmatched requests.

#### Specificity tests

Cover:

- Exact host versus wildcard host.
- Exact path versus wildcard path.
- Wildcard path specificity comparisons.
- Explicit method versus omitted method.
- Multiple simultaneously matching rules.
- Equal-specificity ties.
- Independent results when loading sets in different orders.

#### Conflict tests

Cover:

- Identical rules with different classes.
- Overlapping wildcard rules with different classes.
- Conflicts inside one set.
- Conflicts across multiple sets.
- Duplicate rules with the same class.
- Overlapping rules where one has higher specificity.
- Rules matching different hosts that should not conflict.

#### Normalization and security tests

Cover:

- Host casing.
- Host ports.
- Trailing host dots.
- Host suffix bypass attempts.
- Malformed userinfo.
- HTTP method casing.
- Invalid method tokens.
- Empty paths.
- Query strings.
- Fragments.
- Duplicate slashes.
- Trailing slashes.
- Literal dot segments.
- Encoded dot segments.
- Encoded path separators.
- Invalid percent sequences.
- Unicode paths.
- Arbitrary malformed input.

#### Robustness tests

Use property-based testing or fuzz-style generated inputs to confirm:

- `classify()` never panics.
- Classification remains deterministic.
- Rule ordering does not affect results.
- Malformed input does not unexpectedly map to a valid action class.
- Concurrent classification does not mutate shared state.

Maintain all four existing example tests.

### 18. Multi-agent development plan

Two coding agents are working concurrently.

#### Agent 1 — Configuration and compilation

Ownership:

- `config.rs`
- Parsing and configuration validation tests
- Configuration-related error design
- Validated rule construction
- Loader-related conflict detection integration

Responsibilities:

- Deserialize TOML.
- Reject invalid configurations.
- Verify allowed action classes.
- Build validated mapping data.
- Prepare source metadata for errors.
- Coordinate compiled rule interfaces with the matcher.

Do not independently implement request matching.

#### Agent 2 — Normalization and matching

Ownership:

- `normalize.rs`
- `matcher.rs`
- Normalization and matching unit tests

Responsibilities:

- Implement request normalization.
- Implement exact and wildcard matching.
- Implement specificity ordering.
- Implement overlap detection primitives.
- Expose interfaces for compiled rule evaluation.

Do not independently parse TOML.

#### Integration phase

After both agents finish:

- Review both module contracts.
- Establish shared compiled-rule types.
- Connect parser output to matcher input.
- Implement the public `load()` function.
- Implement the public `classify()` function.
- Connect conflict detection to loading.
- Run integration tests.
- Resolve mismatches between modules.
- Verify order independence and security assumptions.

Use separate Git worktrees or branches for parallel agents where possible, and integrate intentionally rather than allowing simultaneous edits to shared files.

### 19. Verification and acceptance criteria

The implementation is complete when:

- The original public API is unchanged.
- All valid TOML mapping sets load successfully.
- Invalid configurations produce useful errors.
- Only predefined action classes can be returned.
- Multiple mapping sets work without ordering precedence.
- Conflicting rules are rejected.
- The most specific matching rule is selected deterministically.
- Request normalization is consistent and documented.
- Malformed inputs return `None` without panicking.
- Classification requires no network, filesystem, or external services.
- `Classifier` is safe for concurrent use.
- The four starter tests pass.
- Additional unit and integration tests pass.
- The crate builds without warnings.
- Clippy reports no warnings under the selected lint configuration.

Run:

```bash
cargo fmt --check
cargo build
cargo test
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

### 20. Submission requirements

Preserve the complete raw coding-agent session transcripts for all sessions used during development.

Include all instruction files provided to the agents, including any `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or skill files created for this project.

Do not sanitize, redact, or summarize the required raw transcripts.

Review the recorded sessions for unintended exposure of credentials before using any external services during development. Avoid introducing secrets into the take-home workflow.

Ensure the repository and any accompanying documentation accurately describe the implemented behavior and its limitations.

### 21. Final engineering principles

The solution should prioritize:

1. Correctness over cleverness.
2. Security over permissive matching.
3. Deterministic behavior over implicit precedence.
4. Explicit validation over silent correction.
5. Immutable state over shared mutable runtime state.
6. Clear module boundaries over unnecessary abstraction.
7. Comprehensive adversarial testing over happy-path testing alone.

The ultimate goal is a small, production-quality classification component whose behavior can be explained and defended for every supported input.

**The classifier is not expected to understand an agent's reasoning. It must reliably classify observable HTTP operations according to explicitly configured mapping rules.**

Nothing is ignored right now. Untracked items:

| Path | What to do |
|---|---|
| `Firma_take_home/target/` | **Ignore.** It's build output and must not be committed. |
| `Firma_take_home/Cargo.lock` | **Commit it.** It pins dependency versions so reviewers get the same build. |
| `Arch.md` | **Commit it.** It's an instruction file you gave the agents, which the README lists as a deliverable. |
| `agents.md` | **Commit it,** but it's **empty (0 bytes)**. Fill it in or delete it; an empty instruction file will look odd to reviewers. |

A root `.gitignore` with these two lines covers it:
```
target/
.DS_Store
```
Session transcripts live in `~/.claude/projects/...`, outside the repo, so they need no ignore rule. Arch.md describes two concurrent agents, so remember to submit **every** session's raw `.jsonl`.

## Current state
- Three commits: initial, config parser, then normalization and matching. There's also uncommitted work in `src/config.rs`, which makes config validation reuse the `normalize::` functions and adds tests.
- `cargo build` gives no warnings. `cargo test` passes all 22 tests: 18 unit tests and the 4 examples.
- `cargo clippy` reports **3 `collapsible_if` warnings**. Arch.md §19 requires `clippy -D warnings`, so those need fixing.
- The design closely follows Arch.md: separate config, normalize and matcher modules; specificity ordered host, then path, then method; load-time conflict detection using a glob-overlap check; and malformed input returns `None`.

## Review findings
I ran a throwaway test against the code (since deleted) to confirm these:

1. **Bypass through percent-encoded letters (security bug).** With rules `/v1/*` → `payment.read` and `/v1/refunds/*` → `payment.refund`:
   - `/v1/refunds/x` gives `payment.refund`, which is correct.
   - `/v1/%72efunds/x` gives **`payment.read`**, but servers decode it to `/v1/refunds/x`.

   Percent-encoded letters, digits and `-._~` mean the same as the plain characters (RFC 3986). The fix is to decode those, and uppercase the remaining hex escapes, for both requests and patterns.
2. **Lowercase methods fall through to a broader rule.** `DELETE` matches the `DELETE` rule (`payment.refund`), but `delete` matches the method-less rule (`payment.read`). The browser `fetch` API uppercases `delete/get/head/options/post/put` before sending, and "matched as an HTTP client would send them" points that way. Arch.md §7 says "do not silently uppercase", so this is a deliberate decision worth revisiting: at least normalize those six methods.
3. **The same fall-through happens with `//` and trailing slashes.** `/v1//refunds/x` gives `payment.read`. Many servers collapse `//`. Fail-closed handling alone doesn't help here, because a broader rule catches the request. Either collapse them or reject the request, and be ready to defend the choice in the interview.
4. **`rules = []` is accepted.** Removing `#[serde(default)]` only rejects a *missing* `rules` key; an explicitly empty list still loads. Arch.md §7 says to reject empty rule sets.
5. **Errors don't say which file or rule.** Arch.md §14 asks errors to name the mapping set's index and name. Also, rule indexes count per set in `config.rs` but across all sets in `lib.rs:55`, so the same rule can show different numbers depending on where the error comes from.
6. **Smaller items:**
   - `pattern_path` silently drops `?` and `#` from rule paths. `/v1/*?debug=true` becomes `/v1/*`, which goes against "explicit validation over silent correction".
   - The subdomain check allows dotted values like `a.b`, while Arch.md says a single label.
   - `remove_dot_segments` gets quadratically slower with path length (about 21 ms for a 64 KB path in a release build). That's fine at normal URL sizes; consider capping path length.
   - The test files Arch.md planned (`tests/config_validation.rs`, `classification.rs`, `conflicts.rs`, `security.rs`) don't exist yet. There are also no tests for cross-set conflicts, load-order independence, or concurrent use through `Arc`.

I'd fix #1–#3 first; they're the kind of bypass this exercise is built to catch. Want me to add the `.gitignore` and start on them?

content.text:
I fixed the two path bypasses and the lowercase-method bypass, plus a few smaller items. All checks are now clean: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build` (0 warnings), `cargo test` (30 tests pass) and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`. Nothing is committed yet.

**The three fixes:**

1. **Percent-encoded letters** (`src/normalize.rs`): rule and request paths now get the same normalization. Escapes for letters, digits and `-._~` are decoded, so `%72efunds` becomes `refunds`; other escapes are only uppercased. Each path is decoded once, so `%252e` stays a literal `%252e` and isn't turned into `..`.
2. **Lowercase methods:** methods in both rules and requests are now uppercased, so `delete` matches the `DELETE` rule instead of falling through to the broader rule.
3. **`//` and trailing slashes:**
   - Paths containing `//`, a backslash, a space or a control character now come back unclassified, and rule paths containing them are rejected.
   - A path ending in `/` is classified both with and without the slash. If the two answers differ, `classify` returns `None` (deny). With a `/v1/payouts` → `payment.create` rule, `/v1/payouts/` is denied instead of falling through to the broader `/v1/*` → `payment.read` rule.

**Also done:**
- Root `.gitignore` with `target/` and `.DS_Store`.
- `rules = []` is now rejected.
- Rule paths containing `?` or `#` are now rejected instead of being silently cut short.
- Removing `..` and `.` from paths now takes linear time; it used to get quadratically slower with path length.
- The 3 clippy warnings are fixed.
- New `tests/security.rs` with 7 tests that reproduce each bypass through the public API, plus updated unit tests.

**Decisions for you:**
- **`Arch.md` now contradicts the code in two places:** §7/§9 say "do not silently uppercase methods" and "preserve duplicate slashes". I changed both on purpose, so update `Arch.md` to match before you submit; the reviewers will compare them.
- **Trade-off on #3:** a legitimate request to `/v1/refunds/` is now denied when `/v1/refunds/*` and `/v1/*` give different classes. I chose deny because the cost is rare false denials, not misclassified requests. It's a good point to defend in the interview.
- **Still open:** errors don't say which mapping set they came from, rule numbering differs between the two error paths, and subdomains like `a.b` are allowed. There are also no tests yet for conflicts between sets, load order or concurrent use.
- **Still to do:** `agents.md` is still empty, and `Arch.md`, `Cargo.lock` and `.gitignore` are untracked, along with the earlier uncommitted `config.rs` work.

Want me to commit this, or work through the open items first?

content.content:
1	AGENTS.md — Firma HTTP Action Classifier
2	Mission and source of truth
3	Build the Rust library described in README.md: parse TOML mapping sets and classify (method, host, path) into one of the existing ACTION_CLASSES, or None. This is a library, not an HTTP proxy, agent harness, policy engine, UI, network service, or LLM. Never add I/O, networking, databases, or a CLI.
4	
5	Read README.md, Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, and tests/example.rs before editing. The project design document describes our chosen implementation policies; the repository README and the fixed API take precedence if there is any disagreement. Record and surface ambiguities rather than inventing undocumented API behavior.
6	
7	Public API signatures are fixed:
8	pub async fn load(sets: &[&str]) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;
9	impl Classifier {
10	    pub async fn classify(&self, method: &str, host: &str, path: &str) -> Option<&str>;
11	}
12	Keep ACTION_CLASSES unchanged. Keep all four supplied example tests passing. LoadError can be redesigned but must implement std::error::Error. No unwrap/expect on untrusted inputs; classify must never panic. The classifier must be immutable after load, Send + Sync, and fast to query.
13	Workflow: two parallel owners, one integrator, one reviewer
14	Use two concurrent implementation agents. A third agent (Integrator) works after both are ready; an optional fourth (Security Reviewer) inspects the merged result without simultaneously editing it. Do not run multiple agents with write access to the same worktree.
15	
16	Prefer separate Git worktrees and branches:
17	# Run from the repository root; example names only.
18	git worktree add ../firma-config -b agent/config
19	git worktree add ../firma-matcher -b agent/matcher
20	Agent 1 — Configuration, validation, and compilation input
21	Owns: src/config.rs and configuration-focused tests (tests/config_validation.rs or module-local tests). Can propose—but not unilaterally edit—shared public types or src/lib.rs.
22	
23	Responsibilities:
24	- Deserialize mapping sets and rules with Serde; #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on both.
25	- Validate format version (1), required/nonempty fields, allowed action classes, host/subdomain/method/path syntax, and empty rules as defined in the design.
26	- Parse all provided TOML strings, with no filesystem reads; collect source identifiers (input set index, optional name, rule index).
27	- Expose validated configuration records for Agent 2's compiler/matcher representation.
28	- Design structured load errors, including cross-set conflict diagnostics; coordinate error implementation with the Integrator.
29	- Ensure set order never establishes precedence.
30	- Do not create a separate host/path matcher or overlap algorithm in config.rs.
31	Deliver: exported types/functions and tests; notes for Integrator documenting validation invariants, error metadata, and unresolved interface needs.
32	Agent 2 — HTTP normalization, matching, and overlap primitives
33	Owns: src/normalize.rs, src/matcher.rs, and their focused tests. Do not edit src/config.rs; avoid modifying src/lib.rs or Cargo.toml without agreeing on an integration interface.
34	
35	Responsibilities:
36	- Implement safe request normalization (host, method, path) and reject malformed/ambiguous requests with no panic.
37	- Implement compiled exact/wildcard host, method, and path matching.
38	- Define deterministic, documented specificity ordering independent of set order.
39	- Provide rule-overlap detection using the same semantics as runtime matching. Overlap must account for valid normalized request inputs, not just string equality.
40	- Expose a stable interface for validated rules and/or compilation; do not parse TOML.
41	- Write specificity, wildcard, Unicode, adversarial input, and property/fuzz-style tests where practical.
42	Deliver: exported types/functions and tests; notes for Integrator documenting matching semantics, overlap guarantees, and unsupported inputs.
43	Integrator — after both implementation branches land
44	Owns: src/lib.rs, integration adjustments to shared types, Cargo.toml if required, and cross-module tests (tests/classification.rs, tests/conflicts.rs, tests/security.rs). One integration owner only.
45	
46	Responsibilities:
47	- Reconcile module interfaces (do not maintain duplicate canonicalization or matching logic).
48	- Implement the fixed load() function: parse -> validate -> compile -> detect conflicts -> return immutable classifier.
49	- Implement the fixed classify() function: normalize -> find matching compiled rules -> select highest specificity -> return static class or None.
50	- Use source locations from config to generate actionable LoadError variants.
51	- Reject equal-specificity overlapping rules with different classes; allow same-class duplicates and overlaps where one rule has greater specificity. Be conservative when exact overlap cannot be proved: reject unsupported/ambiguous patterns rather than silently accept potential conflicts.
52	- Ensure the same canonicalization contract is applied to rule literals and request inputs.
53	- Run all tests and verify Send + Sync, deterministic set-order behavior, and no warnings.
54	Security Reviewer — after integration (read-only first)
55	Independently review the completed implementation for bypasses, specificity ambiguities, normalization differences between load and classify, panic paths, excessive allocations, unsupported upstream HTTP semantics, and configuration conflicts. Produce reproducible failing tests or concrete findings before requesting targeted fixes. Do not rewrite the architecture without a demonstrated defect.
56	Shared behavior contract
57	These are chosen policies from the technical design, not all explicit README requirements. If a policy conflicts with a direct README requirement, follow README and flag the difference.
58	
59	Hosts: Case-insensitive ASCII DNS hostnames; lower-case for comparison. Request host may have a valid numeric port and one trailing DNS dot; reject empty labels, malformed ports, userinfo, unsupported IP literals, and ambiguous syntax. Match on label boundaries, never arbitrary suffixes. In configuration, host is the base hostname; omitted subdomain matches only the bare host; an exact subdomain = "api" matches only api.base; subdomain = "*" matches any nonempty sequence of subdomain labels but not the bare host.
60	
61	Methods: HTTP tokens are case-sensitive (GET differs from get); reject malformed/empty method tokens. Omitted rule method matches any valid method.
62	
63	Paths: Empty request path normalizes to /; nonempty path must begin /. Drop query/fragment before matching; preserve duplicate and trailing slashes. Normalize unambiguous literal or encoded dot segments consistently; reject invalid percent encoding and ambiguous encoded separators (such as %2F, %5C). Do not blindly decode or double-decode. A configured path must start with /; omission matches all valid paths; * matches zero or more characters including /, and multiple wildcards are supported. /v1/refunds/* matches /v1/refunds/ but not /v1/refunds.
64	
65	Specificity: Lexicographic ranking: (1) exact subdomain over wildcard for subdomain requests (bare-host rules only match bare host), (2) exact path > wildcard path > absent path; among wildcards, more literal characters > fewer wildcards > longer literal prefix, (3) explicit method > absent method. Never use file or insertion order to break ties. If any remaining equal-specificity rules could classify the same valid request differently, reject the configuration during load.
66	
67	Important security boundary: Matching URL metadata cannot reveal agent reasoning, authorization, request body, or provider-specific server decoding rules. Do not infer missing information. If normalization is ambiguous, return None for requests or reject the rule when loading. Document important limits.
68	Module contracts and coordination
69	Before writing a cross-module type, Agent 1 and Agent 2 should agree on:
70	1. The validated rule shape: base host, optional subdomain, optional method, optional path, action_class, and source-location metadata.
71	2. Which module owns compile-time canonicalization of configured host/path values. normalize.rs owns canonicalization semantics; config.rs calls shared helpers rather than duplicating them.
72	3. How matcher.rs accepts rule data and returns match/specificity results.
73	4. How it checks potential overlap with equal specificity, and how the caller gets enough context to construct errors.
74	5. Error behavior for invalid rules vs invalid request inputs.
75	Agent 1 may compile to a small validated configuration IR; Agent 2 may compile that IR to an internal matching IR. Avoid cyclic imports. A practical dependency direction is config -> normalize for shared validation helpers, then lib orchestrates config and matcher; avoid config <-> matcher cycles. Shared DTO types can live in config.rs or a small model.rs owned by the Integrator.
76	
77	When an interface is unresolved, write down a proposed contract and stop at your module boundary, rather than touching the other agent's files. Communicate:
78	- proposed exported type and function signatures;
79	- invariant guaranteed at that boundary;
80	- test that demonstrates intended behavior;
81	- any uncertainty that needs a single integration decision.
82	Error reporting
83	Favor thiserror variants that identify mapping set index, mapping name when known, rule index where applicable, invalid field/value, and the reason for rejection. Since load() accepts TOML text rather than paths, do not claim a file name is known. Conflicts report both rules' source locations. No silent correction of invalid config.
84	Tests and completion gates
85	Each agent runs its focused tests before commit. Only the Integrator claims full-project success. After integration, run from Firma_take_home/:
86	cargo fmt --all -- --check
87	cargo build

AGENTS.md — Firma HTTP Action Classifier
Mission and source of truth
Build the Rust library described in README.md: parse TOML mapping sets and classify (method, host, path) into one of the existing ACTION_CLASSES, or None. This is a library, not an HTTP proxy, agent harness, policy engine, UI, network service, or LLM. Never add I/O, networking, databases, or a CLI.

Read README.md, Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, and tests/example.rs before editing. The project design document describes our chosen implementation policies; the repository README and the fixed API take precedence if there is any disagreement. Record and surface ambiguities rather than inventing undocumented API behavior.

Public API signatures are fixed:
pub async fn load(sets: &[&str]) -> Result<Classifier, LoadError>;
impl Classifier {
    pub async fn classify(&self, method: &str, host: &str, path: &str) -> Option<&str>;
}
Keep ACTION_CLASSES unchanged. Keep all four supplied example tests passing. LoadError can be redesigned but must implement std::error::Error. No unwrap/expect on untrusted inputs; classify must never panic. The classifier must be immutable after load, Send + Sync, and fast to query.
Workflow: two parallel owners, one integrator, one reviewer
Use two concurrent implementation agents. A third agent (Integrator) works after both are ready; an optional fourth (Security Reviewer) inspects the merged result without simultaneously editing it. Do not run multiple agents with write access to the same worktree.

Prefer separate Git worktrees and branches:
# Run from the repository root; example names only.
git worktree add ../firma-config -b agent/config
git worktree add ../firma-matcher -b agent/matcher
Agent 1 — Configuration, validation, and compilation input
Owns: src/config.rs and configuration-focused tests (tests/config_validation.rs or module-local tests). Can propose—but not unilaterally edit—shared public types or src/lib.rs.

Responsibilities:
- Deserialize mapping sets and rules with Serde; #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on both.
- Validate format version (1), required/nonempty fields, allowed action classes, host/subdomain/method/path syntax, and empty rules as defined in the design.
- Parse all provided TOML strings, with no filesystem reads; collect source identifiers (input set index, optional name, rule index).
- Expose validated configuration records for Agent 2's compiler/matcher representation.
- Design structured load errors, including cross-set conflict diagnostics; coordinate error implementation with the Integrator.
- Ensure set order never establishes precedence.
- Do not create a separate host/path matcher or overlap algorithm in config.rs.
Deliver: exported types/functions and tests; notes for Integrator documenting validation invariants, error metadata, and unresolved interface needs.
Agent 2 — HTTP normalization, matching, and overlap primitives
Owns: src/normalize.rs, src/matcher.rs, and their focused tests. Do not edit src/config.rs; avoid modifying src/lib.rs or Cargo.toml without agreeing on an integration interface.

Responsibilities:
- Implement safe request normalization (host, method, path) and reject malformed/ambiguous requests with no panic.
- Implement compiled exact/wildcard host, method, and path matching.
- Define deterministic, documented specificity ordering independent of set order.
- Provide rule-overlap detection using the same semantics as runtime matching. Overlap must account for valid normalized request inputs, not just string equality.
- Expose a stable interface for validated rules and/or compilation; do not parse TOML.
- Write specificity, wildcard, Unicode, adversarial input, and property/fuzz-style tests where practical.
Deliver: exported types/functions and tests; notes for Integrator documenting matching semantics, overlap guarantees, and unsupported inputs.
Integrator — after both implementation branches land
Owns: src/lib.rs, integration adjustments to shared types, Cargo.toml if required, and cross-module tests (tests/classification.rs, tests/conflicts.rs, tests/security.rs). One integration owner only.

Responsibilities:
- Reconcile module interfaces (do not maintain duplicate canonicalization or matching logic).
- Implement the fixed load() function: parse -> validate -> compile -> detect conflicts -> return immutable classifier.
- Implement the fixed classify() function: normalize -> find matching compiled rules -> select highest specificity -> return static class or None.
- Use source locations from config to generate actionable LoadError variants.
- Reject equal-specificity overlapping rules with different classes; allow same-class duplicates and overlaps where one rule has greater specificity. Be conservative when exact overlap cannot be proved: reject unsupported/ambiguous patterns rather than silently accept potential conflicts.
- Ensure the same canonicalization contract is applied to rule literals and request inputs.
- Run all tests and verify Send + Sync, deterministic set-order behavior, and no warnings.
Security Reviewer — after integration (read-only first)
Independently review the completed implementation for bypasses, specificity ambiguities, normalization differences between load and classify, panic paths, excessive allocations, unsupported upstream HTTP semantics, and configuration conflicts. Produce reproducible failing tests or concrete findings before requesting targeted fixes. Do not rewrite the architecture without a demonstrated defect.
Shared behavior contract
These are chosen policies from the technical design, not all explicit README requirements. If a policy conflicts with a direct README requirement, follow README and flag the difference.

Hosts: Case-insensitive ASCII DNS hostnames; lower-case for comparison. Request host may have a valid numeric port and one trailing DNS dot; reject empty labels, malformed ports, userinfo, unsupported IP literals, and ambiguous syntax. Match on label boundaries, never arbitrary suffixes. In configuration, host is the base hostname; omitted subdomain matches only the bare host; an exact subdomain = "api" matches only api.base; subdomain = "*" matches any nonempty sequence of subdomain labels but not the bare host.

Methods: HTTP tokens are case-sensitive (GET differs from get); reject malformed/empty method tokens. Omitted rule method matches any valid method.

Paths: Empty request path normalizes to /; nonempty path must begin /. Drop query/fragment before matching; preserve duplicate and trailing slashes. Normalize unambiguous literal or encoded dot segments consistently; reject invalid percent encoding and ambiguous encoded separators (such as %2F, %5C). Do not blindly decode or double-decode. A configured path must start with /; omission matches all valid paths; * matches zero or more characters including /, and multiple wildcards are supported. /v1/refunds/* matches /v1/refunds/ but not /v1/refunds.

Specificity: Lexicographic ranking: (1) exact subdomain over wildcard for subdomain requests (bare-host rules only match bare host), (2) exact path > wildcard path > absent path; among wildcards, more literal characters > fewer wildcards > longer literal prefix, (3) explicit method > absent method. Never use file or insertion order to break ties. If any remaining equal-specificity rules could classify the same valid request differently, reject the configuration during load.

Important security boundary: Matching URL metadata cannot reveal agent reasoning, authorization, request body, or provider-specific server decoding rules. Do not infer missing information. If normalization is ambiguous, return None for requests or reject the rule when loading. Document important limits.
Module contracts and coordination
Before writing a cross-module type, Agent 1 and Agent 2 should agree on:
1. The validated rule shape: base host, optional subdomain, optional method, optional path, action_class, and source-location metadata.
2. Which module owns compile-time canonicalization of configured host/path values. normalize.rs owns canonicalization semantics; config.rs calls shared helpers rather than duplicating them.
3. How matcher.rs accepts rule data and returns match/specificity results.
4. How it checks potential overlap with equal specificity, and how the caller gets enough context to construct errors.
5. Error behavior for invalid rules vs invalid request inputs.
Agent 1 may compile to a small validated configuration IR; Agent 2 may compile that IR to an internal matching IR. Avoid cyclic imports. A practical dependency direction is config -> normalize for shared validation helpers, then lib orchestrates config and matcher; avoid config <-> matcher cycles. Shared DTO types can live in config.rs or a small model.rs owned by the Integrator.

When an interface is unresolved, write down a proposed contract and stop at your module boundary, rather than touching the other agent's files. Communicate:
- proposed exported type and function signatures;
- invariant guaranteed at that boundary;
- test that demonstrates intended behavior;
- any uncertainty that needs a single integration decision.
Error reporting
Favor thiserror variants that identify mapping set index, mapping name when known, rule index where applicable, invalid field/value, and the reason for rejection. Since load() accepts TOML text rather than paths, do not claim a file name is known. Conflicts report both rules' source locations. No silent correction of invalid config.
Tests and completion gates
Each agent runs its focused tests before commit. Only the Integrator claims full-project success. After integration, run from Firma_take_home/:
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo build
cargo test
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
Minimum coverage: original four tests; unknown keys; missing/empty fields; version; action classes; hosts/methods/paths; nested wildcard subdomains; multiple wildcards; exact/wildcard/omitted precedence; identical and overlapping cross-set conflicts; normalization and bypass attempts; Unicode/malformed inputs; no panic; order independence; parallel requests. If a command fails due to another branch not yet integrated, report this precisely without claiming success.
Agent process and submission evidence
Preserve all raw agent session transcripts for every development session and every agent, including tool calls and instructions. Submit any AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md, and notes provided to agents, as required by README. Do not summarize, sanitize, or redact the required transcript. Never place secrets in prompts or logs; keep credentials out of the project.

At the end of each agent's work, report: changed files, exported interfaces, tests run and results, design decisions, unresolved questions, and branch/commit identifier. Do not claim work from another branch has been tested until it is merged.
